_doc: Per-species showcase layer read by scripts/art/brief.py. `signature` lists the features that must be unmistakable in every image, each with the visual cue that sells it. `pose` is one fixed composition chosen so the signatures are in view. `hidden` names anatomy keys the pose is allowed to conceal. Every key in the record's physiology.anatomy must be either a signature, listed in `visible`, or listed in `hidden`; brief.py refuses to build otherwise.

thirstaserp.identity: A large cobra with a thick scaled body and no legs. Its head is the smooth flat wedge of a real cobra, wider than the neck, with small eyes, no brow ridges, no horns, no ear frills, no crest and no spikes; a broad flaring hood spreads behind the head.

signature.cue: the tail is raised high and shaking its rattle: a stack of hollow bead segments at the tip, with three short curved motion lines on either side of it to show the vibration
the jaws are wide open, showing two long curved fangs, each as long as the head is deep, with a drop of venom hanging from one tip

visible.jaws: the open jaws with the hood flared behind the head
visible.tail: the tail curving up out of the coils to the raised rattle

thirstaserp.pose: Side view: the front third rears up on the left with the hood flared and the jaws open toward the right, the body lies in two coils beneath it, and the tail rises on the right of the frame with the rattle held up at the height of the head.

frackworm.identity: A colossal segmented burrowing worm, as long as a building is tall, with a thick armored hide and no legs, arms, fins, eyes or face.

signature.cue: the whole front end is a drill bit: a pointed cone made of stacked spiral screw threads, ridge after ridge winding around the cone to the point, and the point is split into three wedge jaws that gape open

a ring of narrow slot-shaped pressure nozzles around the neck just behind the drill cone, each nozzle blasting a short fan of sand in straight lines; there are no round holes, no eyes and no face anywhere on the body

visible.body: a long thick tube of many ring segments, tapering to a blunt tail, thicker than a tree trunk relative to its length
visible.hide: heavy plated hide marked by the ring segments

frackworm.pose: Side view: the worm drives upward at a steep angle from the lower right toward the upper left, the drill head at the upper left with its jaws open, the vents spraying sand along the neck, the body curving back down toward the lower right, a few shattered rock chips flying around the head.

poses.foreground-head: Composition with strong depth: the drill head is huge in the foreground at the upper left, filling nearly half the frame, its jaws open toward the viewer and its screw threads and nozzles drawn large and clear. The body recedes behind it into the distance, each ring segment smaller than the one before, curving away in a long hook to a small blunt tail at the lower right. The head is the focus; the body is the background.
poses.depth-two-thirds: Perspective composition. The drill head is closest to the viewer and takes up about two thirds of the artwork: it sits large at the upper left with its jaws open toward the viewer and its screw threads and nozzles clearly readable. Behind the head the body recedes into the distance in perspective: each ring segment is drawn smaller than the one in front of it, so the body shrinks as it snakes away and ends in a small tail far behind. The whole creature is one continuous shape, still a flat black silhouette on white, with no ground, no horizon and no shading; the diminishing segment sizes alone show that this worm is enormous and long.
poses.depth-long-body: Perspective composition. The drill head is closest to the viewer and takes up about two thirds of the artwork: it sits large at the upper left with its jaws open toward the viewer and its screw threads and nozzles clearly readable. Behind the head a very long body of at least twenty ring segments snakes away into the distance in an S-curve, in perspective: each ring segment is drawn smaller than the one in front of it, so the body shrinks steadily as it recedes and ends in a tiny blunt tail far behind, near the lower right. One continuous flat black silhouette on white, no ground, no horizon, no shading; the diminishing segments alone show that this worm is enormous and long.
